name: Salicylic acid
lead: Salicylic acid (2-hydroxybenzoic acid, C7H6O3) is a lipophilic beta hydroxy acid that occurs naturally in willow bark and other plants and is also made industrially. It is a metabolite and chemical precursor of acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) and is a plant defense hormone [1][2]. In dermatology and cosmetics it is used as a keratolytic, meaning an agent that helps the outer layer of skin shed, and it appears in washes, toners, leave-on treatments, medicated pads, wart treatments, dandruff shampoos and chemical peels [1][3].

In looksmaxxing and bodybuilding settings it is discussed chiefly as an over-the-counter acne and blackhead ingredient, including for body acne and for ingrown hairs after shaving. Because it dissolves in oil, proponents describe it as able to work inside pores, and it is often mentioned alongside benzoyl peroxide and retinoids [4][5].

The 2024 American Academy of Dermatology acne guideline makes a conditional recommendation for topical salicylic acid, a lower grade than the strong recommendations it gives for benzoyl peroxide, topical retinoids, topical antibiotics and oral doxycycline [6]. Cosmetic-strength products are generally regarded in the sources reviewed as low-risk when used on small areas, although salicylate toxicity has been documented with very large-area, high-concentration application [1].

paras: Salicylic acid is an ingredient in cleansers, toners, spot treatments and exfoliating products aimed at blackheads, whiteheads, oily skin and rough texture. It also appears in products for keratosis pilaris and seborrhoeic dermatitis, and in body washes used for back and chest acne [1][7][8].

Chemical peels with salicylic acid are used by dermatologists for superficial resurfacing. A 2024 review of peels in melasma describes salicylic acid, alongside glycolic acid, trichloroacetic acid, Jessner's solution, retinoic acid and lactic acid, as an adjunctive or maintenance option for that pigmentation disorder [9]. A broader review of hydroxy acids describes them as widely used anti-aging ingredients [10].

Men's forums such as T Nation include posts in which users say they apply a salicylic acid astringent after shaving to help with ingrown hairs, or use salicylic acid and benzoyl peroxide body washes for back acne, including acne that users attribute to testosterone therapy [11][12][13].

As a medication, salicylic acid is used to remove the outermost layer of skin in conditions such as warts, psoriasis, acne vulgaris, ringworm, dandruff and ichthyosis, and in calluses, corns and acanthosis nigricans [1]. US over-the-counter labels list acne treatment as an indication and carry an external-use-only warning [14].

In acne, the 2024 AAD guideline, which used a formal systematic review and GRADE evidence rating, issued a conditional recommendation for topical salicylic acid alongside clascoterone and azelaic acid. Strong recommendations in the same document went to benzoyl peroxide, topical retinoids, topical antibiotics and oral doxycycline [6]. A conditional recommendation indicates that the guideline panel judged the certainty of evidence or the balance of benefit and harm to be less clear-cut than for the strongly recommended options.

Smaller recent studies have continued to examine it. A 2025 prospective 21-day study evaluated a salicylic acid-containing gel for acne management and skin barrier function [15][16]. A 2023 randomized split-face trial combined a fractional carbon dioxide laser with supramolecular salicylic acid for dense comedones and reported on clearance speed in the title of the paper [17]. A 2022 registered trial compared 25 percent trichloroacetic acid with 30 percent salicylic acid peels in mild to moderate acne [18].
Topical use commonly causes dryness, peeling and irritation, as described in product labeling and dermatology references. US labels carry an external-use-only warning [14].

Wikipedia reports that cosmetic applications pose no significant risk, and that even with several salicylic acid products used together, estimated plasma concentrations stayed well below those permitted for aspirin; on that basis it concludes that salicylic acid cosmetics are safe in pregnancy. The same source notes that toxicity from salicylates is most often due to oral overdose and describes a documented case in which a patient applied a 40 percent salicylate ointment over more than 40 percent of body surface area and then required hemodialysis [1]. Salicylic acid is also listed in the US EPA chemical inventory as an experimental teratogen [1].

Some people are sensitive to dietary salicylates and may develop asthma, rhinitis or gastrointestinal symptoms, which is why low-salicylate diets exist [1]. The European Union limits salicylic acid in cosmetics to defined maximum concentrations, with separate limits for rinse-off hair products, leave-on products and use as a preservative [1].

Applied to skin, salicylic acid is described as causing epidermal cells to detach more readily, which prevents pore blockage and makes room for new cell growth [1]. Grokipedia, an AI-generated source, similarly describes keratolytic, antifungal and anti-inflammatory properties, tied to its ability to penetrate lipid-rich skin layers [19]. As an inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-1 it can reduce prostaglandin formation, which underlies the anti-inflammatory activity of salicylates [1]. Wikipedia also notes that salicylates may retard wound healing, probably through effects on mucopolysaccharide synthesis [1].

Salicylic acid is a phenolic plant hormone involved in growth, photosynthesis and ion transport, and most prominently in defense against pathogens, including systemic acquired resistance [1][2][20]. This large body of plant biology research concerns the molecule's biological role in plants rather than its cosmetic use.

Salicylic acid is a white crystalline solid bearing a hydroxyl and a carboxyl group on adjacent positions of a benzene ring. Commercially it is produced by the Kolbe-Schmitt reaction, in which sodium phenolate reacts with carbon dioxide under pressure and heat and the product is then acidified [1][19]. Acetylation of salicylic acid gives aspirin, and derivatives include methyl salicylate (oil of wintergreen), choline salicylate and bismuth subsalicylate [1].

Willow bark and other salicylate-containing plants have been used medicinally across many cultures, with references in ancient Egyptian, Sumerian and Assyrian texts, and in Native American practice. Archaeologists reported traces of salicylic acid on seventh-century pottery fragments from Colorado in 2014 [1]. Wikipedia notes that the often-repeated claim that Hippocrates used willow as a painkiller is a modern myth, while Grokipedia repeats the association [1][19].

The Reverend Edward Stone reported in 1763 that willow bark reduced fever. Johann Andreas Buchner named salicin in 1828, Henri Leroux isolated a larger amount in 1829, and Raffaele Piria then converted it to salicylic acid [1]. Hermann Kolbe developed an industrial synthesis in 1860, and Bayer's aspirin followed in 1899 according to Grokipedia [19].

In the EU, salicylic acid is controlled under Annex III of the Cosmetics Regulation (EC) 1223/2009, with maximum concentrations that differ by product type [1]. In the US, it is an over-the-counter acne active; the source label examined here is a retail acne product [14].

Among the community material reviewed, salicylic acid appears mostly in lifting and bodybuilding forums rather than as a headline product. Posters mention it as an inexpensive, widely available acne step, often paired with benzoyl peroxide, and some say it only modestly flattened cystic lesions that a dermatologist also treated with retinoids [12][21]. Others report that salicylic acid cleansers left their skin red, dry or burning [22].

Human research on salicylic acid is extensive for dermatologic indications. The 2024 AAD acne guideline gives it a conditional recommendation [6]. A 21-day prospective study of a salicylic acid gel in acne, and a split-face randomized trial combining salicylic acid with a CO2 laser for comedones, are among recent published trials [15][17]. An older randomized trial examined hydroquinone cream with or without salicylic acid peels for photodamage of the neck and upper chest [23]. A 1986 trial of a 5-fluorouracil and salicylic acid preparation (Solcoderm) in basal cell carcinoma found residual tumor islands in two thirds of 24 patients, and its authors advised restricting use to superficial tumors [24].

Registered trials include comparisons of salicylic acid with cryotherapy or pyruvic acid for plantar warts, with silymarin cream for acne, with clotrimazole for otomycosis, and with trichloroacetic acid peels for acne [18][25][26][27][28][29]. Combination products with mometasone were registered for psoriasis [30]. A 2026 single-arm trial of saline immersion for refractory plantar warts cites salicylic acid, cryotherapy and laser as the existing destructive treatments [31].

lore.intro: On T Nation and similar men's fitness forums, salicylic acid is discussed as a cheap over-the-counter fix for body acne, testosterone-related acne and ingrown hairs [12][13].

claims.claim: Salicylic acid washes and sprays clear back and chest acne
claims.believers: Posters report that salicylic acid and benzoyl peroxide body washes left their back clear after they changed their diet, and others use salicylic acid sprays after showering [11][21].
claims.experts: The 2024 AAD guideline gives topical salicylic acid a conditional recommendation for acne, with strong recommendations reserved for benzoyl peroxide, retinoids, topical antibiotics and oral doxycycline [6].

claims.claim: A salicylic acid astringent helps prevent ingrown hairs after shaving
claims.believers: One poster says that combining a specific shaving product with a salicylic acid astringent stopped ingrown hairs [13].
claims.experts: The sources reviewed describe salicylic acid as a keratolytic that helps skin shed, but no published trial in them tests ingrown hairs specifically [1].

claims.claim: Salicylic acid is a mild fix that helps with testosterone-induced acne
claims.believers: Users on testosterone therapy recommend benzoyl peroxide and salicylic acid as over-the-counter options [12].
claims.experts: Guidelines cover acne generally; the sources reviewed contain no trial of salicylic acid specifically in androgen-therapy acne [6].

claims.claim: Salicylic acid washes sometimes worsen or burn skin
claims.believers: One poster says anti-acne washes containing salicylic acid made skin redder, drier and burning [22].
claims.experts: Dryness, peeling and irritation are the common adverse effects of topical salicylic acid, and labels carry external-use warnings [1][14].

claims.claim: Salicylic acid speeds recovery by dissolving dead skin
claims.believers: A training log describes salicylic acid as regenerating skin by dissolving dead cells so new skin appears sooner [32].
claims.experts: Mechanistic descriptions confirm keratolytic action; the sources reviewed also note that salicylates may slow wound healing [1].
